newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor stock falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Accor stock falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in French hotel group Accor fell on Thursday on profit-taking on their gains ahead of the 1996 results announced late on Wednesday, brokers said.

They said investors were pleased with the 14.6 percent rise in net attributable profit to 1.06 billion francs -- slightly above market expectations -- but disappointed with the drop in operating profit to 2.58 billion francs from 2.92 billion due to a weak spending and tourism climate in the first half of 1996.
Accor's stock was down 1.47 percent at 870 francs at 1200 GMT after gaining nearly 100 francs in the past three weeks.
"The results were pretty much in line with expectations, so profit-taking is natural," a portfolio manager said.

Brokerage Massonaud said Accor's stock was correctly valued now and lowered its recommendation to 'hold' from 'buy'. Paribas Capital Markets remains a buyer, and it and Dupont Denant expect the share to outperform the market.
